outcome: Cerebrospinal fluid type I interferons (interferon-alpha, interferon-beta)
White matter lesions on diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging
cohort: The study included 23 newborns with rotavirus-associated leukoencephalopathy (patient group) and 39 infants under 90 days-of-age without the condition (control group).
finding: Newborns with rotavirus-associated leukoencephalopathy exhibited significantly higher cerebrospinal fluid interleukin-6 and interferon-gamma levels compared to controls, with interleukin-6 levels correlating positively with the extent of white matter lesions.
cross-section timing: Newborns and infants under 90 days of age
